domain: Science Policy / Professional Ethics / Technology Governance
topic_summary: The Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics (June 2026) is a policy statement by 16 mathematicians addressing how AI technologies threaten core values of mathematical practice: proof integrity, attribution, research autonomy, proper evaluation, and ethical responsibility. It provides recommendations for individuals, institutions, funders, and industry to preserve mathematical values while engaging with AI tools.

key_entities: Leiden Declaration working group (16 mathematicians from 15 universities, convened September 2025)
Technology companies (Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Axiom, Math Inc.) (AI developers using mathematics for training/publicity)
Mathematical community (130+ signatories at publication, including Fields medalist Peter Scholze)
Academic publishers and journals (gatekeepers of peer review)
National Science Foundation ICARM (U.S. institute supporting AI adoption in mathematics)
Formal proof verification systems (AlphaProof, Gauss, agentic systems)
Mathematical commons (published papers, formal libraries used as training data)
key_tensions: Proof integrity vs AI plausibility (correct proofs vs unreliable but plausible AI-generated arguments)
Research autonomy vs commercial priorities (expert-driven significance vs AI-amenable problems)
Attribution norms vs training data practices (proper citation vs unlicensed corpus scraping)
Peer review timelines vs market publicity (community evaluation vs press release announcements)
key_mechanisms: Peer review system (journals, proceedings, books as validation mechanism)
Attribution system (credit to human authors, responsibility for correctness)
Training data extraction (systematic use of published mathematics without consent for model training)
key_absences: Enforcement mechanism for disclosure requirements (declaration provides recommendations but no binding compliance structure)
Quantitative threshold for what constitutes 'significant' AI use requiring disclosure

axes.human_readable: Proof Verification Crisis (AI Plausibility vs Mathematical Certainty)
axes.structural_delta: AI systems generate plausible but unreliable arguments indistinguishable from correct proofs without formal verification
axes.primary_observable: Rate of retracted AI-assisted proofs; proportion of submissions requiring formal verification; reviewer time per paper
axes.selection_reason: Foundational mountain: epistemic integrity is the substrate on which all other mathematical values depend

axes.human_readable: Attribution Erosion (Training Data Extraction vs Citation Norms)
axes.structural_delta: AI models trained on mathematical commons return outputs without proper citation, violating attribution norms
axes.primary_observable: Proportion of AI-generated outputs with complete citations; copyright violation complaints; licensing opt-out rates
axes.selection_reason: Tangled_rope with highest centrality: extraction mechanism that benefits AI developers while undermining merit-based credit system

axes.human_readable: Review System Collapse (Peer Review vs Press Release Publicity)
axes.structural_delta: Results announced via press releases on market timelines before peer review can occur
axes.primary_observable: Time lag between press release and peer-reviewed publication; proportion of announced results never published; reviewer burden metrics
axes.selection_reason: Snare mechanism: commercial publicity timelines trap mathematics in evaluation bypass loop

axes.human_readable: Research Autonomy Capture (Expert Judgment vs AI-Amenable Problems)
axes.structural_delta: Research priorities shift from expert-judged significance to problems amenable to automated methods
axes.primary_observable: Funding allocation to AI-amenable vs expert-prioritized problems; hiring criteria emphasizing AI tool use; problem selection in major journals
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis node with highest centrality: captures the cumulative effect of multiple extraction mechanisms on disciplinary autonomy

axes.human_readable: Asymmetric Collaboration Terms (Industry Resources vs Academic Bargaining Power)
axes.structural_delta: Mathematicians collaborate with industry under asymmetric terms due to resource disparities and precarious academic employment
axes.primary_observable: Proportion of industry collaborations with IP restrictions; academic salary stagnation vs industry offers; access to computational resources
axes.selection_reason: Structural rope enabling autonomy capture: resource asymmetry creates coordination problem independent of other axes

axes.human_readable: Dual-Use Complicity (Mathematical Reasoning Training vs Harmful Applications)
axes.structural_delta: Mathematical theorem proving used to train general-purpose AI deployed in warfare, surveillance, and democracy-undermining applications
axes.primary_observable: Proportion of math-trained models deployed in military/surveillance contracts; mathematician participation in dual-use projects; ethical review adoption rates
axes.selection_reason: Piton of atrophied ethical oversight: mathematicians historically treated their work as value-neutral, now face complicity in harmful applications

axes.human_readable: Formalization Translation Gap (Computer-Encoded vs Human Presentation)
axes.structural_delta: Difficulty in translating between formal proof encodings and human-readable mathematical concepts
axes.primary_observable: Error rate in human-to-formal translations; proportion of formalized proofs requiring human verification; translation time per proof
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: captured as component of proof_verification_crisis mountain; translation gap is mechanism within broader verification challenge

axes.human_readable: Early-Career Disproportionate Impact (Established vs Emerging Researchers)
axes.structural_delta: AI disruptions disproportionately affect students and early-career mathematicians who lack established reputations
axes.primary_observable: Hiring rates for early-career mathematicians; PhD completion rates; career trajectory changes post-AI adoption
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: distributional consequence of research_autonomy_capture rather than independent structural axis

omegas.description: Declaration provides recommendations but no binding enforcement. Are disclosure requirements Rope (voluntary coordination) or Scaffold (aspirational without teeth)? Effectiveness depends on professional organization adoption.
What constitutes 'significant' AI use requiring disclosure? Declaration leaves threshold undefined. Without operational definition, compliance becomes subjective and unverifiable.
Is proof_verification_crisis a true Mountain (inherent epistemic limits of AI) or Piton (current technical limitations)? Future formal verification advances may reclassify.
At what point does mathematical contribution to general AI training constitute complicity in harmful applications? Declaration asserts responsibility but provides no decision procedure.

Declaration recommends public computational infrastructure as alternative to proprietary systems. Is this Rope (coordination solution) or Scaffold (underfunded aspiration)? Depends on government funding commitment.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: proof_verification_crisis classified as mountain (inherent epistemic limits) but may be piton (current technical state). Future advances in formal verification could reclassify. Generated omega_mountain_reclassification to bound this uncertainty.
